analogs.name: Tso Kar Basin
analogs.biome: Alpine Cold Desert / High-Altitude Saline Wetland

geology.rock_units: Quaternary alluvium, lacustrine clay-silt deposits, crystalline salt crusts

analog_processes: Cold-climate evaporative desiccation of saline paleolakes
Cryogenic sulfate and borate mineral precipitation
Periglacial polygon formation under extreme freeze-thaw cycling
Astrobiological biosignature preservation in cryogenic evaporites
planetary_analog_relevance.fidelity_summary: High fidelity for Martian cold-climate lacustrine desiccation and cryogenic permafrost polygon dynamics. High UV and low atmospheric pressure provide realistic Mars surface stressors.

data_confidence.verification_status: In-situ field surveyed (ISRO / Geological Survey of India / Wadia Institute)

references.citation: Bhattacharya et al. (2021). Astrobiological potential of high-altitude hypersaline Tso Kar lake, Ladakh, India. Planetary and Space Science, 205, 105280.
Ray et al. (2021). Morphological and mineralogical study of Ladakh as a Martian analog. Current Science, 120(5), 844-855.
ISRO Space Applications Centre (2022). High-Altitude Planetary Analog Missions in Ladakh: Geomorphic and Astrobiological Atlas.

analogs.name: Lonar Crater
analogs.biome: Semi-Arid Basaltic Impact Basin / Soda Lake

geology.lithology_type: Hypervelocity Impact Crater in Continental Flood Basalt
geology.rock_units: Deccan Traps tholeiitic basalts (~65 Ma), impact ejecta blanket, suevite, allochthonous breccia
geomorphic_features: Simple crater morphology (1.88 km diameter, 150 m depth)
Continuous hummocky ejecta blanket extending 1.5 crater radii

planetary_analog_relevance.primary_target: Lunar Mare & Martian Basaltic Impact Structures
analog_mission_targets: Artemis III/IV Lunar South Pole Highland/Mare Boundaries
analog_processes: Hypervelocity impact cratering mechanics in pristine basaltic targets
Solid-state diaplectic phase transformation (Maskelynite formation at 25-45 GPa)
Post-impact hydrothermal alteration of basaltic ejecta
Microbial colonization of basaltic impact-melt glass under alkaline conditions
planetary_analog_relevance.fidelity_summary: Exceptional, globally unique terrestrial analog. One of only four known hypervelocity impact structures on Earth in basaltic bedrock. Directly models lunar mare and Martian volcanic crater morphology and shock petrology.

data_confidence.verification_status: Extensively verified by drilling, micro-Raman, TEM, and thermal infrared spectroscopy

references.citation: Fredriksson, K. et al. (1973). Lonar Lake, India: An impact crater in basalt. Science, 180(4088), 862-864.
Wright, S. P. et al. (2011). Thermal infrared spectroscopy of shocked basalt at Lonar Crater, India: Analogs for Martian crater ejecta. J. Geophys. Res. Planets, 116(E9).
Kieffer, S. W. (1977). Impact conditions required for formation of melt and maskelynite in basalt: Lonar Crater, India. The Moon, 16(3), 301-332.

geology.rock_units: Proterozoic Aravalli metamorphic basement, thick Quaternary saline lacustrine silt and mud
geomorphic_features: Extensive planar salt-crust playa (230 sq km)
Desiccation mud-cracks and salt tepee structures

analog_processes: Evaporative concentration and fractional crystallization in terminal basins
Biomolecule and lipid entrapment in fluid inclusions within halite crystals
Seasonal moisture cycling on hyper-saline crust integrity
Pigmented haloarchaeal survival strategies under high UV exposure
planetary_analog_relevance.fidelity_summary: Strong geomorphic and geochemical analog for ancient Martian chloride-bearing plains and lacustrine shoreline evaporites where past biological markers may be entrained in halite crystals.

data_confidence.verification_status: Geological Survey of India sediment core verified

references.citation: Sinha, R., & Raymahashay, B. C. (2004). Evaporite mineralogy and geochemical evolution of Sambhar Lake, Rajasthan. J. Geol. Soc. India, 64, 417-424.
Yadav, A. et al. (2022). Halophilic and haloalkaliphilic microbial diversity of Sambhar Salt Lake and its astrobiological implications. Extremophiles, 26(3), 21.

geology.rock_units: Cenozoic alluvial-lacustrine gravels, volcanic ash ignimbrite layers, massive nitrate ore deposits (caliche)
geomorphic_features: Paleochannels inactive for millions of years

analog_processes: Atmospheric deposition and preservation of perchlorate salts
Dry limit of microbial cellular replication (aw < 0.60)
Photocatalytic organic degradation under intense solar UV irradiation
Subsurface endolithic colonisation within translucent halite rocks
planetary_analog_relevance.fidelity_summary: Gold standard terrestrial analog for the dry limit of life, regolith perchlorates, and oxidative decomposition processes on the Martian surface.

data_confidence.verification_status: Extensively documented across 30+ NASA & ESA field campaigns

references.citation: Navarro-González, R. et al. (2003). Mars-like soils in the Atacama Desert, Chile, and the dry limit of microbial life. Science, 302(5647), 1018-1021.
Parro, V. et al. (2011). SOLID3: A multiplex immunoassay biosensor for life detection in the Atacama Desert. Astrobiology, 11(10), 969-996.

geology.lithology_type: Dry Polar Permafrost and Glacial Tills
geology.rock_units: Beacon Supergroup quartzose sandstones, Ferrar Dolerite sills, relict dry till blankets
geomorphic_features: Dry permafrost (dry-frozen active layer with ice table at depth)

planetary_analog_relevance.primary_target: Martian Polar Layered Deposits & Permafrost Regolith
analog_processes: Ice sublimation and vapor diffusion through cryogenic porous regolith
Cryptoendolithic microbial communities sheltered inside porous sandstones
Katabatic wind erosion creating ventifacts and lag gravels
Deep cold permafrost coring and drill mechanical testing
planetary_analog_relevance.fidelity_summary: Top terrestrial analog for sub-surface ground ice dynamics, thermal contraction crack polygons, and extreme cold-dry limits on Mars polar plains.

data_confidence.verification_status: NSF Long Term Ecological Research (LTER) verified

references.citation: McKay, C. P. et al. (1998). Antarctic dry valleys as a model for Martian polar terrain. Planetary and Space Science, 46(2-3), 209-224.
Marchant, D. R., & Head, J. W. (2007). Antarctic Dry Valleys: Microclimate zonation, variable geomorphic processes, and implications for assessing climate change on Mars. Icarus, 192(1), 187-222.

geology.lithology_type: Tholeiitic Flood Basalts, Calderas & Subglacial Palagonite
geology.rock_units: Holocene basaltic lava fields (a'a and pahoehoe), palagonite tuffs (hyaloclastites), pumice tephra layers
geomorphic_features: Extensive basaltic lava flows with collapse pits and lava tubes

planetary_analog_relevance.primary_target: Lunar Mare & Martian Basaltic Volcanic Plains
analog_processes: Effusive basaltic volcanism and lava tube formation (subsurface astronaut shelter analogs)
Palagonitization of basaltic glass via volcano-ice hydrothermal interactions
Aeolian transport and physical sorting of basaltic sand grains
Geological field training and autonomous rover traverse testing
planetary_analog_relevance.fidelity_summary: Historical and active testbed for Apollo and Artemis astronaut geology training. High mineralogical fidelity for unevolved basaltic crusts on both Moon and Mars.

data_confidence.verification_status: NASA Apollo historical training site & NASA PSTAR program verified

references.citation: Mangold, N. et al. (2011). Hydrothermal alteration in basaltic environments on Mars and Earth: Lessons from Iceland. Astrobiology, 11(8), 755-772.
Stockstill-Cahill, K. R. et al. (2012). Palagonitization of basaltic tephra in Iceland: An analog for Martian surface alteration. J. Geophys. Res., 117.
